title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tried New England clam chowder and a Dunkin' Munchkin on stage at Xfinity Center in Mansfield.
Duff has been sampling local foods during her 'The Lucky Me Tour,' showcasing regional tastes at each tour stop.
The singer playfully interacted with the audience, expressing her surprise and delight at the New England specialties.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman will debut for the Boston Red Sox against the Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday.
Rutschman was acquired from the Orioles on Aug. 3 and has recovered from wrist inflammation.
The Red Sox may adjust their roster by optioning Connor Wong or designating Jake Rogers for assignment.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Springfield's The Zoo in Forest Park remains closed after storm damage to enclosures and uprooted massive trees.
Springfield declared a state of emergency with power outages and a building collapse affecting 45 people.
The Zoo faces significant financial impact from closure and repair costs, while no animals were injured.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough, confirmed by Massachusetts State Police.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East was closed Monday evening following the crash.
Drivers are advised to use alternate routes due to expected significant traffic delays in the area.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Shrewsbury police responded to a possible drowning at Lake Quinsigamond on Sunday afternoon.
A male victim was found dead near Sunset Beach early Monday after a search using sonar technology.
The investigation into the drowning is ongoing; the victim's identity has not been released.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, undrafted from the University of Missouri, is impressing in New England Patriots training camp.
Jacobs recorded 47 tackles, 3 sacks, and 2 pass breakups during his 2025 college season at Missouri.
He is emerging as a dynamic linebacker option, showing speed and playmaking in Patriots' thin linebacker corps.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed legislation eliminating gestational limits on abortion, allowing physicians more discretion in Massachusetts abortions past 24 weeks.
The new law, H.5595, prevents medical reviews from overruling physician judgment, aligning Massachusetts with nine other states without gestational limits.
Opponents argue the bill weakens protections for unborn children, while supporters claim it enhances patient access to necessary care.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of a free Black man named Sebastian, also known as Boston, was uncovered at Boston’s Granary Burying Ground.
The stone's inscription, dating from 1729, is the oldest known gravestone for a free Black person in the U.S.
Sebastian, a former slave, influenced early antislavery movements and advocated for marriage rights for enslaved individuals.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to Patriots practice; Campbell participated fully while Davis was limited.
Romeo Doubs and Kyle Williams made notable catches during New England Patriots' training camp practice.
Patriots' joint practice with the Colts scheduled for Tuesday ahead of preseason opener at Gillette Stadium.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard operating a rescue torpedo was pulled underwater by a shark at Scarborough Beach State Park in Maine.
The lifeguard freed himself from the torpedo and swam to shore; the beach closed for an hour afterward.
Scarborough officials advise swimmers to be cautious as shark activity has increased near Scarborough Beach and Higgins Beach.
